set.pinev: Range line R14W/R13W between sec. 36 and sec. 31 (1896 Ogle plat; 1972 USGS Zumbro Lake topo).

src: Standard Atlas of Wabasha County, Minnesota (Geo. A. Ogle & Co., Chicago, 1896), University of Minnesota Borchert Map Library
vs-2064584.st: The 1896 Ogle atlas (Zumbro township) prints SOUTH TROY P.O. at a residence on the west edge of sec. 31, just east of the R14W/R13W range line, with a blacksmith shop to the north. A church is drawn just west of the north-south road at the east edge of sec. 36, and a school at the sec. 31/36 corner to the south. The 1972 topo still shows a church on that spot by the South Troy label. Pin moved onto the crossroads. Church ground is look-only.

tw-wi-new-london-hoffman-orchard.st: The wallet was dug up under an orchard tree on Nordman's Hill, 2 miles south of New London, some weeks before 29 Jan 1908. It is thought to have been buried by a farmhand who called himself "Harry Palmer of Chicago". He vanished, was arrested in Chicago for robbery and killed himself in jail. No owner of the money was ever found.
src: Appleton Post-Crescent, 30 Jan 1908, p. 8 and 6 Feb 1908, p. 2 (local)
